I feel like there's a few sources which are just no reputable. Buzzfeed, daily mail and cracked (amongst many others) are just all about clickbait with no actual content.

While other sites like rt, azzabella (sp?) Reuters and others can not be trusted in regard to particularly western news.

There's also cringe science or conspiracy websites that are just full of shit and not reputable in the very least. Much like a blogspot, anyone can create a website and post anything they want.

These are just a few that I can think of. But basically I can't imagine any of them having anything worth to say.

I just checked the home pages of those sites. I thought I would agree with Daily Mail, but after taking another look, I'm not so sure. While they may not be very credible, neither are so many other sites. What separates those sites? Is it really an issue of quality?

In fact, it seems that all three sites are independent. I am more concerned about multiple sites coming from the same small group of people then independent sites. I have a strong preference for indies as those are where we get the widest range of viewpoints.

Take a look at the top two submissions in v/politics right now. Cracked and Free Beacon.

The Cracked site has all kinds of popular source complaints, while the Free Beacon site has little. If you read through the comments, many of those opposing the Cracked site are also saying this article is pretty good, while there is not much source discussion about the Free Beacon site.

At first, it appears that the Free Beacon site is putting up current news -- and it is. But, if you search those terms, you will find other sources that cover the same story, many with more facts and less slant. Meanwhile, the Cracked article is fairly unique. There's a difference.

The Free Beacon site is part of a very large family of sites all pushing the same agenda. In fact, the editor of Free Beacon was a member of the Republican partisan splinter group PNAC, and also worked with Koch brothers supported National Review. Meanwhile, Cracked does not appear to have such direct or exact political connections.

I think the Free Beacon site, at least in this case, is not as good as the Cracked site, by dirrect comparison. What do you you think?

CLICK BAIT. I suppose any site with advertising could be considered "click bait." This is an area where we can probably come up with a good, hard and fair rule. For example: sites that have pop-ups, pop-unders, running videos, scrollers, back-button redirections, etc. There is a point where the advertising becomes too intrusive. That's what I say is clickbait. Let's say where a site has two or more of these annoyances.
